Row names station names, default taken locationName column deployments. Column names dates. matrix values represent daily effort: NA: camera set day. 1: camera fully active entire day. decimal 0 1: camera partially active (e.g. first last day deployment). title: Camera operation matrix
text: Let’s first extend dataset deployments contains column cameraID sessionID. can specify column containing session IDs added station names using session_col argument. sessionID displayed following camtrapR’s convention: Station__SESS_sessionID: can also specify column containing camera IDs added station names following camtrapR’s convention: Station__CAM_CameraID using camera_col argument: use camera session IDs, camtrapR’s convention Station__SESS_SessionID__CAM_CameraID followed: can also use prefix "Station" station names done camtrapR’s cameraOperation() setting use_prefix = TRUE:
code: x_extended <- x  deployments(x_extended) <- deployments(x) %>%    mutate(sessionID = c(1, 2, 3, 4)) %>%    mutate(cameraID = c(1, 2, 3, 4)) cam_op_with_session_ids <- get_cam_op(   x_extended,   session_col = "sessionID" ) # Since the full matrix would be too wide to display here, we only inspect # the row names: row.names(cam_op_with_session_ids) #> [1] "B_HS_val 2_processiepark__SESS_1"      #> [2] "B_DL_val 5_beek kleine vijver__SESS_2" #> [3] "B_DL_val 3_dikke boom__SESS_3"         #> [4] "B_DM_val 4_'t WAD__SESS_4" cam_op_with_camera_ids <- get_cam_op(   x_extended,   camera_col = "cameraID" ) # Since the full matrix would be too wide to display here, we only inspect # the row names: row.names(cam_op_with_camera_ids) #> [1] "B_HS_val 2_processiepark__CAM_1"      #> [2] "B_DL_val 5_beek kleine vijver__CAM_2" #> [3] "B_DL_val 3_dikke boom__CAM_3"         #> [4] "B_DM_val 4_'t WAD__CAM_4" cam_op_with_session_and_camera_ids <- get_cam_op(   x_extended,   camera_col = "cameraID",   session_col = "sessionID" ) # Since the full matrix would be too wide to display here, we only inspect # the row names: row.names(cam_op_with_session_and_camera_ids) #> [1] "B_HS_val 2_processiepark__SESS_1__CAM_1"      #> [2] "B_DL_val 5_beek kleine vijver__SESS_2__CAM_2" #> [3] "B_DL_val 3_dikke boom__SESS_3__CAM_3"         #> [4] "B_DM_val 4_'t WAD__SESS_4__CAM_4" cam_op_with_session_and_camera_ids_prefix <- get_cam_op(   x_extended,   camera_col = "cameraID",   session_col = "sessionID",   use_prefix = TRUE ) # Since the full matrix would be too wide to display here, we only inspect # the row names: row.names(cam_op_with_session_and_camera_ids_prefix) #> [1] "StationB_HS_val 2_processiepark__SESS_1__CAM_1"      #> [2] "StationB_DL_val 5_beek kleine vijver__SESS_2__CAM_2" #> [3] "StationB_DL_val 3_dikke boom__SESS_3__CAM_3"         #> [4] "StationB_DM_val 4_'t WAD__SESS_4__CAM_4"

title: Detection history matrix
text: get_detection_history() returns list three elements: detection_history, effort, dates. output argument controls detection history matrix contains. Three options available: Binary (output = "binary"): 1 species detected station occasion, 0 : Number observations (output = "n_observations"): number records per station per occasion. default get_record_table() settings, duplicate records day station removed, equivalent "binary" cases: readability, detection_history element shown : allow counts 1 "n_observations", build record table without removing duplicates: Number individuals (output = "n_individuals"): number individuals detected per station per occasion, summed across records:

text: Load packages used example: example function example_dataset() used load example Camera Trap Data Package dataset. dataset derived study detecting invasive muskrat coypu populations using camera traps. making visualization map_summary(), Camera Trap Data Package dataset transformed grouped data frame. can done using function summarize_observations() summarize_deployments(), depending aspect dataset want visualize. demonstrated example. Let’s also create Camera Trap Data Package dataset filtered specific species. , can first inspect species detected. function taxa() gives overview unique scientific names within Camera Trap Data Package dataset: example filters Anas platyrhynchos. can filter using filter_observations() function:
code: library(camtraptor) #>  #> Attaching package: 'camtraptor' #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     contributors library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union x <- example_dataset() summ_obs <- x %>%   summarize_observations(group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude"))  summ_depl <- x %>%   summarize_deployments(group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude")) taxa(x) #> # A tibble: 10 × 5 #>    scientificName     taxonID  taxonRank vernacularNames.eng vernacularNames.nld #>    <chr>              <chr>    <chr>     <chr>               <chr>               #>  1 Anas platyrhynchos https:/… species   mallard             wilde eend          #>  2 Anas strepera      https:/… species   gadwall             krakeend            #>  3 Ardea              https:/… genus     great herons        reigers             #>  4 Ardea cinerea      https:/… species   grey heron          blauwe reiger       #>  5 Aves               https:/… class     bird sp.            vogel               #>  6 Homo sapiens       https:/… species   human               mens                #>  7 Martes foina       https:/… species   beech marten        steenmarter         #>  8 Mustela putorius   https:/… species   European polecat    bunzing             #>  9 Rattus norvegicus  https:/… species   brown rat           bruine rat          #> 10 Vulpes vulpes      https:/… species   red fox             vos x_anas_p <- x %>%    filter_observations(scientificName == "Anas platyrhynchos")  summ_obs_anas_p <- x_anas_p %>%   summarize_observations(group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude"))

title: Visualize deployment features
text: can visualize number detected species deployment using function map_summary() feature set n_scientificName:
code: summ_obs %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_scientificName")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: visualize number events observed, set feature = n_events:
code: summ_obs %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_events")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: visualize number observations, set feature = n_observations: can also visualize number observations specific species: argument extend set TRUE within summarize_observations() function, deployments without observations Anas platyrhynchos also visualized black multiplication symbol ×:
code: summ_obs %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_observations") summ_obs_anas_p %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_observations") # Make grouped data frame by summarizing summ_obs_anas_p_extend <- x_anas_p %>%   summarize_observations(     group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude"),      extend = TRUE   )  # Visualize summ_obs_anas_p_extend %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_observations")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: visualize number observed individuals, set feature = sum_count: observations, can also visualize number observed individuals specific species:
code: summ_obs %>%   map_summary(feature = "sum_count") summ_obs_anas_p %>%   map_summary(feature = "sum_count")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: Note: Notice package RAI normalized deployment activity period 100 days. visualize Relative Abundance Index (RAI) given species (e.g. Anas platyrhynchos), set feature = "rai_observations". RAI based number observations, see next section calculate RAI number detected individuals.
code: summ_obs_anas_p %>%   map_summary(feature = "rai_observations")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: Note: Notice package RAI normalized deployment activity period 100 days. can also visualize RAI based number detected individuals instead number observations (see previous section). Set feature = "rai_count":
code: summ_obs_anas_p %>%   map_summary(feature = "rai_count")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: can visualize duration deployments, also called effort, number active hours using grouped data frame created summarize_deployments() section ‘Setup’. Set feature = "effort_duration": units ‘hour’ (default) can also used, using argument effort_unit. example, can express effort days:
code: summ_depl %>%   map_summary(feature = "effort_duration") summ_depl %>%   map_summary(feature = "effort_duration", effort_unit = "day")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: can happen deployments didn’t detect recognizable animal (scientificName = NA) didn’t observe anything (deployments observations). visualizing number species, two situations shown default black red multiplication symbols × respectively: hide deployments unknown species deployments observations, set na_values_show zero_values_show FALSE respectively.
code: # Create a data package demonstrating two scenarios: # 1. Deployments with observations of unknown species (black ×) # 2. Deployments with no observations at all (red ×)  # Keep only observations with unknown species x_unknown <- x %>%   filter_observations(is.na(scientificName))  # Remove all observations from deployment "00a2c20d" # to simulate a deployment with no observations at all x_unknown <- x_unknown %>%   filter_observations(deploymentID != "00a2c20d")  # Summarize, extend = TRUE ensures deployments with no observations are included summary_obs_unknown <- x_unknown %>%   summarize_observations(     group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude"),     extend = TRUE   )  # Visualize summary_obs_unknown %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_scientificName")

title: Visualize deployment features
text: can control variables displayed hovering deployment using hover_columns argument. can choose among columns grouped data frame created summarize_observations() summarize_deployments(). example deploymentID number observations shown hovering: Deactivating cluster mode hovering also possible:
code: summ_obs %>%   map_summary(     feature  = "n_observations",     hover_columns = c("deploymentID", "n_observations")   ) summ_obs %>%    map_summary(feature = "n_observations", cluster = FALSE, hover_columns = NULL)

title: Visualize deployment features
text: default color palette viridis color palette called "inferno". can specify another viridis color palette, e.g. "viridis" "magma", RColorBrewer palette, e.g. "BuPu" "Oranges". viridis color palette used: can use palette RColorBrewer, e.g. "BuPu" palette: Another easy way specify palette create passing vector colors names hex color codes, e.g. c("black", "blue", "#A3675F"):
code: summ_obs %>%    map_summary(feature = "n_observations", palette = "viridis") summ_obs %>%    map_summary(feature = "n_observations", palette = "BuPu") summ_obs %>%    map_summary(     feature = "n_observations",     palette = c("black", "blue", "#A3675F")   )

what: Use a specific icon and color for zero values
title: Visualize deployment features
text: can customize icon shown zero-value deployments passing icon URL zero_values_icon_url size pixels zero_values_icon_size. Many free icon libraries available online, icons8. following example uses custom icon size 50 pixels: Typically colour part URL. example change color default icon green (2ECC71): Modifying default value ("black") can useful color deployments zero values can sometimes similar one colors used palette.
code: x_anas_p %>%   summarize_observations(     group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude"),     extend = TRUE   ) %>%   map_summary(     feature = "n_observations",     zero_values_icon_url = "https://img.icons8.com/color/48/000000/futurama-fry.png",     zero_values_icon_size = 50   ) x_anas_p %>%   summarize_observations(     group_by = c("deploymentID", "latitude", "longitude"),     extend = TRUE   ) %>%   map_summary(     feature = "n_observations",     zero_values_icon_url = "https://img.icons8.com/ios-glyphs/30/2ECC71/multiply.png"   )

title: Visualize deployment features
text: can also modify upper lower limit circle sizes specifying radius_range (default:c(10,50)):
code: summ_obs %>%    map_summary(feature = "n_observations", radius_range = c(20, 150))

title: Visualize deployment features
text: default upper limit color palette radius defined based actual feature values. However, sometimes can useful set absolute upper limit. can done setting argument relative_scale FALSE specifying upper limit max_scale. Upper limit lower number observations: Upper limit higher number observations:
code: summ_obs %>%    map_summary(     feature = "n_observations",     relative_scale = FALSE,     max_scale = 2   ) summ_obs %>%    map_summary(     feature = "n_observations",     relative_scale = FALSE,     max_scale = 50   )

title: Workflow
text: Load package:
code: library(camtraptor) #>  #> Attaching package: 'camtraptor' #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     contributors

title: Workflow
text: start data analysis first need data. , function example_dataset() used load example Camera Trap Data Package dataset included camtraptor package. dataset derived study detecting invasive muskrat coypu populations using camera traps. read locally stored dataset, use read_camtrapdp(): vignette example dataset used.
code: x <- example_dataset() x <- read_camtrapdp("path/to/datapackage.json")

title: Workflow
text: Now read data, can start exploring . Camtrap DP dataset consists three tables: deployments, media observations. details data structure, see Camtrap DP website. can access table directly using deployments(), media() observations(). Let’s take look deployments table: get quick overview species recorded, use taxa():
code: deployments(x) #> # A tibble: 4 × 24 #>   deploymentID locationID locationName  latitude longitude coordinateUncertainty #>   <chr>        <chr>      <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>                 <dbl> #> 1 00a2c20d     e254a13c   B_HS_val 2_p…     51.5      4.77                   187 #> 2 29b7d356     2df5259b   B_DL_val 5_b…     51.2      5.66                   187 #> 3 577b543a     ff1535c0   B_DL_val 3_d…     51.2      5.66                   187 #> 4 62c200a9     ce943ced   B_DM_val 4_'…     50.7      4.01                   187 #> # ℹ 18 more variables: deploymentStart <dttm>, deploymentEnd <dttm>, #> #   setupBy <chr>, cameraID <chr>, cameraModel <chr>, cameraDelay <dbl>, #> #   cameraHeight <dbl>, cameraDepth <dbl>, cameraTilt <dbl>, #> #   cameraHeading <dbl>, detectionDistance <dbl>, timestampIssues <lgl>, #> #   baitUse <lgl>, featureType <fct>, habitat <chr>, deploymentGroups <chr>, #> #   deploymentTags <chr>, deploymentComments <chr> taxa(x) #> # A tibble: 10 × 5 #>    scientificName     taxonID  taxonRank vernacularNames.eng vernacularNames.nld #>    <chr>              <chr>    <chr>     <chr>               <chr>               #>  1 Anas platyrhynchos https:/… species   mallard             wilde eend          #>  2 Anas strepera      https:/… species   gadwall             krakeend            #>  3 Ardea              https:/… genus     great herons        reigers             #>  4 Ardea cinerea      https:/… species   grey heron          blauwe reiger       #>  5 Aves               https:/… class     bird sp.            vogel               #>  6 Homo sapiens       https:/… species   human               mens                #>  7 Martes foina       https:/… species   beech marten        steenmarter         #>  8 Mustela putorius   https:/… species   European polecat    bunzing             #>  9 Rattus norvegicus  https:/… species   brown rat           bruine rat          #> 10 Vulpes vulpes      https:/… species   red fox             vos

title: Workflow
text: Now explored dataset, can start filtering. Use filter_deployments() select specific deployment locations filter_observations() select specific species. example, filtering two specific locations mallard (Anas platyrhynchos): filter_deployments() filters deployments table two selected locations, automatically removes associated observations media belong deployments. filter_observations() filters remaining observations keep mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) observations. Want filter timelapse observations? Use filter_out_timelapse() shortcut filter_observations(x, captureMethod != "timelapse").
code: x_filtered <- x %>%   filter_deployments(     locationName == c(       "B_HS_val 2_processiepark",       "B_DM_val 4_'t WAD"       )     ) %>%   filter_observations(scientificName == "Anas platyrhynchos")

title: Workflow
text: visualizing, data first needs summarized. Use summarize_observations() get overview observations per deployment: Use summarize_deployments() get overview deployments:
code: summ_obs_filtered <- summarize_observations(x_filtered) summ_obs_filtered #> # A tibble: 1 × 10 #> # Groups:   deploymentID, latitude, longitude, scientificName [1] #>   deploymentID latitude longitude scientificName     n_scientificName n_events #>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>                         <int>    <int> #> 1 00a2c20d         51.5      4.77 Anas platyrhynchos                1        6 #> # ℹ 4 more variables: n_observations <int>, sum_count <int>, #> #   rai_observations <dbl>, rai_count <dbl> summ_depl_filtered <- summarize_deployments(x_filtered) summ_depl_filtered #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #> # Groups:   deploymentID, latitude, longitude [2] #>   deploymentID latitude longitude effort_duration        #>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl> <Duration>             #> 1 00a2c20d         51.5      4.77 2789044s (~4.61 weeks) #> 2 62c200a9         50.7      4.01 1903602s (~3.15 weeks)

title: Workflow
text: Use map_summary() visualize summary map. Visualize number mallard observations per deployment: can see, one two deployments mallard observed. can also visualize daily effort per deployment:
code: map_summary(summ_obs_filtered, feature = "n_observations") map_summary(summ_depl_filtered, feature = "effort_duration")

title: Workflow
text: practice ’d chain everything single pipeline, e.g.: information visualization, check vignette vignette("visualize-deployment-features").
code: x %>%   filter_deployments(     locationName == c(       "B_HS_val 2_processiepark",       "B_DM_val 4_'t WAD"       )     ) %>%   filter_observations(scientificName == "Anas platyrhynchos") %>%   summarize_observations() %>%   map_summary(feature = "n_observations")

title: Filter out timelapse observations — filter_out_timelapse
text: Subsets observations Camera Trap Data Package object, removing timelapse observations, .e. observations captureMethod = timeLapse. function shortcut filter_observations(x, captureMethod != "timelapse").

title: Filter out timelapse observations — filter_out_timelapse
code: filter_out_timelapse(x)

title: Filter out timelapse observations — filter_out_timelapse
text: x Camera trap data package object, returned camtrapdp::read_camtrapdp().

title: Filter out timelapse observations — filter_out_timelapse
text: x filtered.

what: Get the camera operation matrix — get_cam_op
title: Get the camera operation matrix — get_cam_op
text: function superseded camtrapR now supports reading Camera Trap Data Packages. Use camtrapR::readCamtrapDP() camtrapR::cameraOperation() instead. Creates camera operation matrix returned camtrapR::cameraOperation().

title: Get the camera operation matrix — get_cam_op
code: get_cam_op(   x,   station_col = "locationName",   camera_col = NULL,   session_col = NULL,   use_prefix = FALSE )

title: Get the camera operation matrix — get_cam_op
text: x Camera trap data package object, returned camtrapdp::read_camtrapdp(). station_col Column name use identifying stations. Default: "locationName". camera_col Column name column specifying Camera ID. Default: NULL. session_col Column name use identifying session. Default: NULL. Use creating multi-session / multi-season detection histories. use_prefix Logical (TRUE FALSE). TRUE returned row names start prefix "Station" returned camtrapR::cameraOperation(). Default: FALSE.

title: Get the camera operation matrix — get_cam_op
text: matrix. Row names always indicate station ID. Column names dates.

title: Get the camera operation matrix — get_cam_op
text: deployment data default grouped locationName (station ID camtrapR jargon) another column specified user via station_col argument. multiple deployments linked location, daily efforts higher 1 occur. Partially active days, e.g. first last day deployment, result decimal effort values camtrapR::cameraOperation().

what: Get the detection history of a species — get_detection_history
title: Get the detection history of a species — get_detection_history
text: function superseded camtrapR now supports reading Camera Trap Data Packages. Use camtrapR::readCamtrapDP() camtrapR::detectionHistory() instead. Creates detection history matrix species based record table camera operation matrix. detection history concept developed within camtrapR package, see function documentation camtrapR::detectionHistory(). detection history matrix binary matrix rows represent camera stations columns represent occasions. matrix filled 1s 0s, 1 indicates species detected station given occasion 0 indicates species detected. function also returns effort matrix, contains number days station active occasion, dates matrix, contains dates occasions.

title: Get the detection history of a species — get_detection_history
code: get_detection_history(   recordTable,   camOp,   species,   output,   occasionLength = 1,   minActiveDaysPerOccasion = NULL,   maxNumberDays = NULL,   day1 = "station",   buffer = NULL,   unmarkedMultFrameInput = FALSE )

title: Get the detection history of a species — get_detection_history
text: recordTable data frame camera trap records. data frame contain columns 'Station', 'Date', 'Species' 'n'. 'Station' camera station ID, 'Date' date record, 'Species' species name, 'n' number observations, 'n_ind' number individuals detected. camOp matrix camera operation data. Rows represent camera stations columns represent occasions. matrix contain number days station active occasion. species Character. species name. output Character. type output. Choose one : "binary", "n_observations", "n_individuals". occasionLength Integer. length occasions days. decimals allowed. Default: 1. minActiveDaysPerOccasion Integer. Minimum number active trap days occasions included. Default: NULL. used, must smaller equal occasionLength. maxNumberDays Integer. Maximum number trap days per station. Default: NULL. used, must greater equal occasionLength. day1 Character. Day occasions begin: station setup date ("station") specific date (e.g. "2015-12-31"). multi-season detection history (unmarkedMultFrameInput = TRUE), day1 = "station" allowed. Default: "station". buffer Integer. makes first occasion begin number days station setup. buffer can used combination day1 = "station". Default: NULL. warning returned records removed taken buffer period. unmarkedMultFrameInput Logical. TRUE, function return input multi-season occupancy models unmarked R package (argument y unmarked::unmarkedMultFrame()). Default: FALSE.

title: Get the detection history of a species — get_detection_history
text: list three elements: detection_history: detection history matrix effort: effort matrix dates: dates matrix

title: Get the detection history of a species — get_detection_history
text: function take input Camera Trap Data Package object, camera operation matrix record table, calculated based Camera Trap Data Package object. information, see get_cam_op() get_record_table() functions. camera operation matrix (camOp) created multi-season study (via argument session_col get_cam_op()), session detected automatically. can set unmarkedMultFrameInput = TRUE generate multi-season detection history. row corresponds site, columns season-major, occasion-minor order, e.g. o1_SESS_A, o2_SESS_A, o1_SESS_B, o2_SESS_B, etc.

title: Get the record table — get_record_table
text: function superseded camtrapR now supports reading Camera Trap Data Packages. Use camtrapR::readCamtrapDP() camtrapR::recordTable() instead. Creates record table Camera Trap Data Package tabulating species records. event-based observations corresponding media taken account. record table concept developed within camtrapR package, see article. See also function documentation camtrapR::recordTable(). Note: dates times expressed UTC format.

title: Get the record table — get_record_table
code: get_record_table(   x,   stationCol = "locationName",   exclude = NULL,   minDeltaTime = 0,   deltaTimeComparedTo = NULL,   removeDuplicateRecords = TRUE )

title: Get the record table — get_record_table
text: x Camera trap data package object, returned camtrapdp::read_camtrapdp(). stationCol Character name column containing stations. Default: "locationName". exclude Character vector scientific names excluded record table. Default: NULL. minDeltaTime Time difference records species station considered independent (minutes). Default: 0. deltaTimeComparedTo One "lastIndependentRecord" "lastRecord". two records considered independent, second one must least minDeltaTime minutes last independent record species (deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord"), minDeltaTime minutes last record (deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord"). minDeltaTime 0, deltaTimeComparedTo must NULL (default). removeDuplicateRecords Logical. several records species, e.g. different sex lifeStage, station exactly time, show one? Default: TRUE. Duplicates removed keeping first observation observation table.

title: Get the record table — get_record_table
text: tibble data frame containing species records additional information stations, date, time metadata, filenames directories images (media) linked species records. details columns returned: Station: Character, station names, found deployment column defined parameter stationCol. Species: Character, scientific name observed species. n: Numeric, number observed individuals (renamed count observations table). DateTimeOriginal: Datetime object, found column eventStart observations, UTC format. Date: Date object, date part DateTimeOriginal, UTC format. Time: Character, time part DateTimeOriginal UTC format. delta.time.secs: Numeric, duration seconds previous independent record given species certain location. delta.time.mins: Numeric, duration minutes previous independent record given species certain location. delta.time.hours: Numeric, duration hours previous independent record given species certain location. delta.time.days: Numeric, duration days previous independent record given species certain location. Directory: List, file paths images linked given record, defined column filePath media. Filename: List, file names images linked given record, defined column fileName media. Latitude: Numeric, latitude station, based deploymentID observations. Longitude: Numeric, longitude station, based deploymentID observations. clock: Numeric, clock time radians. solar: Numeric, solar time radians. Calculated using overlap::sunTime, essentially uses approach described Nouvellet et al. (2012) doi:10.1111/j.1469-7998.2011.00864.x .

text: x Camera trap data package object, returned camtrapdp::read_camtrapdp(). feature Feature visualize. One columns generated summarize_deployments() summarize_observations() used grouping. Possible values present output summarize_observations() : n_scientificName: Number detected species. n_events: Number events observed. n_observations: Number observations. sum_count: Number individuals observed. rai_observations: RAI calculated using number observations (n_observations). rai_count: RAI calculated using number observed individuals (sum_count). Possible values present output summarize_deployments() : effort_duration: Deployment effort duration. species Character scientific names. Common names supported anymore camtraptor 1.0.0. Please, check filter_observations() know filter scientificName. "" (default) scientific names automatically selected. NULL observations species taken account. sex Character defining sex class filter , e.g. "female" c("male", "unknown"). NULL (default) observations sex classes taken account. Please, check filter_observations() know filter sex. life_stage Character vector defining life stage class filter , e.g. "adult" c("subadult", "adult"). title: Visualize deployments features — map_summary
text: df Grouped data frame generated summarize_deployments() summarize_observations() eventually subset . columns latitude longitude present df, map can generated error returned. feature Feature visualize. One columns generated summarize_deployments() summarize_observations() used grouping. Possible values present output summarize_observations() : n_scientificName: Number detected species. n_events: Number events observed. n_observations: Number observations. sum_count: Number individuals observed. rai_observations: RAI calculated using number observations (n_observations). rai_count: RAI calculated using number observed individuals (sum_count). Possible values present output summarize_deployments() : effort_duration: Deployment effort duration. effort_unit Time unit use visualizing deployment effort duration. Ignored feature "effort_duration". One : second minute hour day month year  NULL (default), effort returned hours. cluster Logical value indicating whether using cluster option visualizing maps. Default: TRUE. hover_columns Character vector columns df show mouse hover. Use NULL disable hovering. Default: columns df used grouping feature visualize. palette palette name color function values mapped . Default: "inferno". Typically one following: character vector RGB named colors. Examples: c("#000000", "#0000FF", "#FFFFFF")),topo.colors(10)). full name RColorBrewer palette, e.g. "BuPu" "Greens", viridis palette: "viridis", "magma", "inferno" "plasma". options, see parameter palette leaflet::colorNumeric(). zero_values_show Logical indicating whether show deployments zero values. Default: TRUE. See details. zero_values_icon_url Character URL icon showing deployments zero values.  Use NULL zero_values_show FALSE. Default: cross (multiply symbol) "https://img.icons8.com/ios-glyphs/30/000000/multiply.png". See details. zero_values_icon_size number set size icon show groups (e.g. deployments) zero values. Use NULL zero_values_show FALSE. Default: cross (multiply symbol) "https://img.icons8.com/ios-glyphs/30/000000/multiply.png". See details. na_values_show Logical indicating whether show groups (e.g. deployments) observations feature "n_scientificName". Default: TRUE. See details. na_values_icon_url Character URL icon showing groups (e.g. deployments) observations. Used feature "n_scientificName", ignored otherwise. Use NULL na_values_show FALSE. Default: red cross (multiply symbol) "https://img.icons8.com/ios-glyphs/30/FA5252/multiply.png". na_values_icon_size number set size icon showing groups (e.g. deployments) observations. Used feature "n_scientificName", ignored otherwise. Use NULL na_values_show FALSE. Default: 10. relative_scale Logical indicating whether use relative color radius scale (TRUE) absolute scale (FALSE). absolute scale used, specify valid max_scale. max_scale Number indicating max value used map color radius. radius_range Vector length 2 containing lower upper limit circle radius. lower value used deployments zero feature value, e.g. observations, identified species, zero RAI zero effort. upper value used deployment(s) highest feature value (relative_scale = TRUE) max_scale (relative_scale = FALSE). Default: c(10, 50).

title: Read a Camera Trap Data Package — read_camtrap_dp
text: Observations can contain classifications two levels: Media-based observations (observationLevel = "media") based single media file directly linked via mediaID. Event-based observations (observationLevel = "event") based event, defined combination eventID, eventStart eventEnd. event can consist one media files, directly linked . read_camtrapdp() function automatically assign eventIDs media, using media.deploymentID = observations.deploymentID observations.eventStart <= media.timestamp <= observations.eventEnd. Note can result media linked multiple events (thus duplicated), example events sub-events defined.

text: camtraptor now offers step--step workflow explore visualize data: Read Camtrap DP files read_camtrapdp() (reexported camtrapdp::read_camtrapdp()). function supports Camtrap DP 1.0 higher. Filter data filter_deployments(), filter_media() filter_observations() (also reexported camtrapdp). functions replace predicate functions (worked deployments) filter arguments get_ functions. Summarize deployments observations summarize_deployments() summarize_observations(). calculate features (e.g. "effort_duration" "n_events") grouped fields temporal levels choice. Visualize summary tables using map_summary(), creates Leaflet map desired feature. function replaces map_dep(). ’s example read files, filter coordinates adult animals, calculate observation-level summaries, create map showing number individuals: Note can stop explore () summary results returned summarize_observations() selecting one ("sum_count") visualize map_summary(): , use specific get_ function see specific summary result. repeat filters map_dep(): details new workflow can found vignette vignette("workflow").
code: library(camtraptor) file <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tdwg/camtrap-dp/1.0/example/datapackage.json" x <- read_camtrapdp(file) x %>%   filter_deployments(latitude > 51.0, longitude > 5.0) %>%   filter_observations(lifeStage == "adult") %>%   summarize_observations() %>%   map_summary(feature = "sum_count") x %>%   filter_deployments(latitude > 51.0, longitude > 5.0) %>%   filter_observations(lifeStage == "adult") %>%   summarize_observations() #> # A tibble: 4 × 10 #> # Groups:   deploymentID, latitude, longitude, scientificName [4] #>   deploymentID latitude longitude scientificName     n_scientificName n_events #>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>                         <int>    <int> #> 1 29b7d356         51.2      5.66 Anas platyrhynchos                1        3 #> 2 577b543a         51.2      5.66 Martes foina                      1        1 #> 3 577b543a         51.2      5.66 Mustela putorius                  1        3 #> 4 577b543a         51.2      5.66 Vulpes vulpes                     1        1 #> # ℹ 4 more variables: n_observations <int>, sum_count <int>, #> #   rai_observations <dbl>, rai_count <dbl> # Before x <- read_camtrap_dp(file) get_n_individuals(   x,   life_stage = "adult",   pred_and(pred_gt("latitude", 51.0), pred_gt("longitude", 5.0)) ) map_dep(   x,   feature = "n_individuals",   life_stage = "adult",   pred_and(pred_gt("latitude", 51.0), pred_gt("longitude", 5.0)) )

title: camtraptor 1.0.0
text: New summarize_deployments() calculates duration effort. Users can define grouping field(s) (e.g. "locationID") temporal level (e.g. "month") (#366). New summarize_observations() calculates several observation-related features, number taxa, number events, number observations, sum individual counts Relative Abundance Index (RAI). Users can define grouping field(s) temporal level (#367). New map_summary() creates Leaflet map showing selected feature summary table generated summarize_deployments() summarize_observations(). New filter_out_timelapse() allows filter timelapse observations (#306). New add_coordinates() adds deployment coordinates observations (#350). following functions reexported camtrapdp: Filter functions: filter_deployments(), filter_media() filter_observations(). return data package filtered data (#315). Get data functions: deployments(), media(), observations(), locations(), events(), taxa(), individuals(), contributors(). return data frame (#317). Assign data functions: deployments<-, media<-, observations<-, contributors<-. assign data frame back data package used care, can invalidate data package (#328). Example data: example_dataset(). returns minimal example data package (Camtrap DP standard) replaces mica dataset.
